gap: No result ChatGPT got says that BougeRV's 240 Wh detachable LiFePO4 battery fits only the CRH20, CRX3, CRD2 V2.0 and Rocky V3.0 fridges. Neither BougeRV model ChatGPT showed (the plain 23 qt and the CRPRO30) is on that list, while the battery-ready CRX3 23QT sells for $199.99 on BougeRV's store, $30 more than the plain 23 qt.
standout_why: I compared against OutdoorGearLab's Best Electric Coolers page (cited in both chats) and GearJunkie's 9 Best Electric Coolers (top result). OutdoorGearLab lists only the cords each cooler ships with and its battery-protection settings, and says the CFX5 works with 'portable batteries' without naming one. GearJunkie mentions only a 173 Wh snap-in pack for the BougeRV CRD45, the EverFrost 2 40's own battery, and nothing on ICECO or the Dometic PLB40. Neither page says which BougeRV fridges take BougeRV's battery or that the CRPRO30 and plain 23 qt can't. I could not open gearandhome.com (cited in chat 1): the fetch failed on a TLS certificate error and the curl retry was blocked. That cited rival is unread, so I scored 2 rather than 3.
decides: The chats ask 'Need a built-in battery?' but then recommend BougeRV's plain 23 qt ($169.99) and CRPRO30 ($229.99). BougeRV's 240 Wh battery doesn't fit either of them. On the CRPRO30 the battery path is an external 266 Wh power station sold as a kit for $389.99. For a shopper who picks the battery option, the BougeRV pick should be the CRX3 23QT ($199.99) or CRX3 30QT ($249.99), which take the internal 240 Wh battery. For the 45 L tier, ICECO's VL45 has no internal battery. ICECO sells it with a separate 250 Wh 'Magnetic Power Bank' ($663.10 bundle), and only the VL45PLUS ($799) is listed as 'Magnetic Battery Ready'. Dometic's battery for the CFX5 45 is the external PLB40 at $539.99, which almost doubles the cost of the $997 fridge. Of the four, only Dealectric's own Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40L has a removable battery included.
